{{short description|Russian mathematician}}
'''Anton Yurevich Alekseev''' (Антон Юрьевич Алексеев, born 9 August 1967) is a Russian mathematician.

Alekseev was a student of [[Ludvig Faddeev]]. Alekseev worked at the [[Steklov Institute]] in Saint Petersburg and, at the beginning of the 1990s, at [[Uppsala University]], Sweden. He is now a professor ordinarius at the [[University of Geneva]].<ref name=homepage>{{cite web|title=Anton Alekseev, Professeur ordinaire|website=Section of Mathematics, University of Geneva|url=https://www.unige.ch/math/en/people/alekseev/|date=2007-10-03|access-date=2019-11-20|archive-date=2020-09-22|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200922102911/https://www.unige.ch/math/en/people/alekseev/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Alekseev does research on representation theory of [[Lie group]]s and algebras, moment theory, [[symplectic geometry]] and [[mathematical physics]].<ref name=homepage/>

In 2006 he, with [[Eckhard Meinrenken]], published in ''[[Inventiones Mathematicae]]'' a proof of the Kashiwara-Vergne conjecture.<ref name="AlekseevMeinrenken2006">{{cite journal|last1=Alekseev|first1=A.|last2=Meinrenken|first2=E.|title=On the Kashiwara–Vergne conjecture|journal=Inventiones Mathematicae|volume=164|issue=3|year=2006|pages=615–634|issn=0020-9910|doi=10.1007/s00222-005-0486-4|bibcode=2006InMat.164..615A|arxiv=math/0506499|s2cid=119682533}} [https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0506499 arXiv preprint]</ref> In 2008 he gave a new proof with [[:fr:Charles Torossian]].<ref>{{cite arXiv|author=Alekseev, Anton|author2=Torossian, Charles|title=The Kashiwara-Vergne conjecture and Drinfeld's associators|year=2008|eprint=0802.4300|class=math.QA}}</ref>

In 2014 Alekseev was an invited speaker with talk ''Three lives of the Gelfand-Zeitlin integrable system'' at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Seoul.

In 2020 Alekseev received the Medal of the [[Erwin Schrödinger International Institute for Mathematics and Physics]].<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pEelA4kRNcI&pp=ygUORVNJIE1FZGFsIDIwMjA%3D|title = Medal Ceremony and Award Lecture of ESI Medal 2020| website=[[YouTube]] }}</ref>

September 1993, Springer, Lecture Notes in Physics, 1994; [https://inis.iaea.org/search/search.aspx?orig_q=RN:26031544 abstract] {{doi|10.1007/3-540-58453-6}}
**within the ''Proceedings'' by Anton Alekseev and A. Malkin: Symplectic geometry and the Chern-Simons theory, pp.&nbsp;59–97 [https://www.mat.univie.ac.at/~esiprpr/esi080.pdf preprint]
*with Eckhard Meinrenken:  The non commutative Weil Algebra, Inventiones Mathematicae, vol. 139, 2000, pp.&nbsp;135–172, [https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9903052 Arxiv]
*with Eckhard Meinrenken: Poisson geometry and the Kashiwara-Vergne conjecture, C. R. Acad. Sci., 335, 2003, pp.&nbsp;723–728, [https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0209346 Arxiv]
*with Eckhard Meinrenken: Clifford algebras and the classical dynamical Yang-Baxter-Equations, Math.Res.Lett., vol. 10, 2003, pp.&nbsp;253–268, [https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0209347 Arxiv]
*with Eckhard Meinrenken: On the Kashiwara-Vergne conjecture, Inventiones Mathematicae 164, 2006, 615–634, [https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0506499  Arxiv]
*with Carlo A. Rossi, Charles Torossian, [[Thomas Willwacher]]: Logarithms and Deformation Quantization, Inventiones Mathematicae, vol. 206, 2016, pp.&nbsp;1–26, [https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.3200 Arxiv]
*with C. Torossian: The Kashiwara-Vergne Conjecture and Drinfeld's associators, [[Annals of Mathematics]], vol. 175, 2012, pp.&nbsp;415–463, [https://arxiv.org/abs/0802.4300 Arxiv]
*with C. Torossian: On triviality of the Kashiwara-Vergne problem for quadratic Lie algebras,  C. R. Math. Acad. Sci. Paris, vol. 347, 2009, pp.&nbsp;21–22, 1231–1236. [https://arxiv.org/abs/0909.3743 Arxiv]
*with C. Torossian: Kontsevich deformation quantization and  flat connections,  Comm. Math. Phys., vol. 300, 2010, pp.&nbsp;47–64, [https://arxiv.org/abs/0906.0187 Arxiv]
*with B. Enriquez, C. Torossian: Drinfeld associators, braid groups and explicit solutions of the Kashiwara-Vergne equations, Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci., Band 112, 2010, S. 143–189, [https://arxiv.org/abs/0903.4067 Arxiv]
*with Arkady Berenstein, Benjamin Hoffman, Yanpeng Li: Langlands Duality and Poisson-Lie Duality via Cluster Theory and Tropicalization, [https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.04104 Arxiv 2018]
